The sources are real and every quoted constant is accurate, but the load-bearing inference is contradicted by the vendor source the claim leans on.  SOURCE AUTHENTICITY — all verified, all accurate: - magico13/PyEmVue exists (240 stars, pushed 2025-12-26). auth.py:10-12 has exactly CLIENT_ID "4qte47jbstod8apnfic0bunmrq", USER_POOL "us-east-2_ghlOXVLi1", region us-east-2. pye
gotchas: This is the OLD path. Emporia's own client names this origin `EMPORIA_LEGACY_API_ORIGIN` and uses it for one call only (device discovery), having moved measurement onto c-api /v1. Expect it to be withdrawn. Nothing in a vendor document promises /AppAPI will keep working.

The one reason to care: `scale=1S` with `instant=` returns 1-second data, which the vendor's v1 power endpoint cannot do (its floor is MINUTES). Vendor and community paths genuinely differ in capability; this is recorded rather than resolved in favour of one.

The Cognito USER_POOL value `us-east-2_ghlOXVLi1` is `community-single` — PyEmVue hardcodes it and Emporia's own config.ts publishes only the client id and the region, not the pool id. emporia-go accepts the pool id as user-supplied configuration and hardcodes nothing, so it does not corroborate the value. unmappedReports: Per-channel usage — getDeviceListUsages/getChartUsage return a value per `channel`, same 19-measurement-to-one-MetricKind collapse as the v1 dialect., `instant` + scale `1S` gives second-resolution power, which the contract has no problem representing as `ac-power`, but there is no MetricKind or contract concept for the sampling resolution itself — and here it is the whole reason to prefer this dialect over the vendor one., Smart plug switching (PUT /devices/outlet) maps to `set-switch`, but on a `switch` DeviceKind — not on any model surveyed here., Thermostats (/customers/thermostats) and EV chargers (/customers/evchargers) have no MetricKind coverage at all; they are outside the contract's device vocabulary., /customers/partners — account/business metadata, correctly has no MetricKind.
